newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-RESEARCH ALERT-Portman rated a buy.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-RESEARCH ALERT-Portman rated a buy.

text.p: Brisbane-based broker Wilson HTM Ltd is recommending Portman Mining Ltd as a buy investment, reflecting the coal producer's capital growth potential.
"Buy Portman Mining for capital growth through 1977," Wilson's director, resources research, Phil Hutchings said in a report.
Hutchings said the group's management was confident that the two million tonnes target of coal shipments this year from the Burton mine in central Queensland would be achieved.
The upside for Portman was the planned expansion of Burton to between four and five million tonnes a year of mainly high-quality coking coal, Hutchings said.
This feasability study was now in progress with initial plans due to be released next month, he said.
"Indicative capital cost is about A$50 million and we estimate that this can be comfortably funded from internal cash flow plus a modest amount of additional debt," Hutchings said.
Once the expansion project was complete, the Burton mine would be among the larger coal mines in Queensland and have a very low operating structure, Hutchings said.
Portman still looked very good value at last Friday's closing price of A$2.42, Hutchings said.
Portman shares were 11 cents firmer at A$2.55 at 3.45 p.m. (0445 GMT) on Monday.

On a comparative basis with QCT Resources Ltd, Queensland's other coking coal producer, Portman's share price had the potential to be revalued to over $4 once the full expansion was up and running, he said.
"Portman is shaping up as a high-yield stock with our forecast dividend of 10 cents for 1977 (unfranked) equating to a 4.2 percent yield," Hutchings said.
